hook: A 1920 bank building in the South End Historic District, marking the site of Jack London's 1876 birthplace.

parcel.note: A commercial (bank) building of 1920 in Class-B non-combustible construction. Business addresses are usually deferred on this site; this page exists because the address was named in the prompting article.

assessment.note: The roll reports land and improvements at the identical figure of $1,489,335. Treat the $2,978,670 total as reliable and the split as unresolved.

historic_status.ceqa_status_label: Historical resource; within an Article 10 and National Register historic district
historic_status.reason: Article 10 Historic District, National Register Historic District, California Register Historic District, Historic Survey Result

historic_district.name: South End Historic District
historic_district.note: The district is Listed (not merely eligible) on the National and California Registers as well as being a local Article 10 district.

permits.description: reroof with hot works; cool-roof material exceeding minimum solar reflectance values
install a new HVAC system for the second floor with rooftop package units and ducted distribution
install a fire alarm to monitor water flow
add two automatic teller machines, no structural changes

narrative.lead: Jack London was born on this site in 1876; the building he was born in is gone, and this one postdates it by four decades.

sections.heading: Assessed value
sections.body: The roll reports land and improvements at the same figure, $1,489,335 each, so no split is charted.

historical_record.description: The source records Jack London as born on this site in 1876, states the original building was destroyed, and notes a small plaque dedicated to him. The building now on the parcel dates from 1920, so it is not the birth structure.
